Subject: Redwood Dedicated — burst behaviour and pricing questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles. We’re working through sizing for Redwood Dedicated and have a few specific asks on burst/autoscale pricing before we finalize the reserved commit. Quick summary: 

- Our initial committed pool would be 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (24/7 baseline). We expect irregular peaks for marketing events that push sustained load for ~2–6 hours, 6–8 times per quarter.
- We care about a predictable per-minute surcharge for sustained bursts, and want clarity on cooldown windows (how long until our burst headroom replenishes).
- Is there a way to offset surge charges if we show a predictable 30–45 day usage pattern (i.e., credit sustained throughput against next month)?

Can you share a concrete surcharge table, example math for a bill with three 4-hour spikes in a month, and whether Redwood will consider a one-time onboarding credit (we have integration costs).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that’s easier.

Sara Long
Head of Procurement, StormApps

Attachments: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Long <sara@stormapps.com>
Cc: Devon Park <cto@stormapps.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 12:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — burst behaviour and pricing questions

Hi Sara — great to hear from you and glad the demo resonated. I’m looping in a short proposal (attached) and a worked example. High level answers first, then the attachment has the per-minute math: 

- Surcharge model: we charge a per-minute "surge rate" for burst GPUs above committed capacity. Default: $2.25 per vGPU-minute (A100-equivalent) for bursts up to 4 hours, then a stepped rate of $3.40/minute for sustained minutes beyond 4 hours in the same event.
- Cooldown: burst headroom replenishes on a rolling 72-hour window by default. We can shorten to 48h for accounts with committed minimums and a 12-month reserved contract.
- Sustained throughput offset: we offer a monthly "sustained offset" credit when customers demonstrate repeatable monthly spike patterns; the credit is applied to next invoice and reduces effective surge minutes by up to 30% (requires a 6-week observational baseline).

Attached: rdw-burst-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf (table + worked example) and a blank forecast sheet you can populate (stormapps-dedicated-burst-qtr-forecast.xlsx). Example math: three 4-hour spikes on top of 8 GPUs -> ~720 surge vGPU-minutes/event * 3 events => billing at base surge rate for first 4 hours. See page 3.

Short next steps: if you’re comfortable with the framework, can you share the quarter forecast (the attached spreadsheet) and whether StormApps can commit to a 12-month reserved tier? That unlocks the 48h cooldown option and a preferred-tier surge rate.

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Redwood Dedicated — burst behaviour and pricing questions — proposed adjustments

Karthik / Lauren — forwarding Sara’s ask and my proposal. Sara called out two negotiable items: (1) a one-time onboarding credit to offset integration costs, and (2) application of sustained throughput offsets earlier than our 6-week baseline, given StormApps can share telemetry. I’ve sketched three concession options in the attached spreadsheet:

Option A — Standard: 72h cooldown, surge $2.25 / vGPU-min (0–4h), $3.40 / vGPU-min (>4h), sustained offset available after 6 weeks.
Option B — Preferred: 48h cooldown, 15% discount on surge rates, sustained offset after 3 weeks, requires 12-mo reserved commit (8 GPUs).
Option C — Enterprise: 36h cooldown, 25% discount on surge rates, 30% sustained offset from month 2, includes a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 1000 vGPU-minutes. Requires exec approval.

I recommend Option B for deal velocity — preserves margin but gives StormApps a clear operational win. If they push for onboarding credit, we can offer a capped credit (e.g., 1,000–2,000 vGPU-minutes) but should gate it on a signed 12-month commitment and a short proof-of-usage export.

Questions: can Legal approve a small capped credit without an SOW? Also, do we have precedent for accelerating sustained-offset to 3 weeks if the customer provides telemetry?

Thanks — Mina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood Dedicated — burst behaviour and pricing questions — proposed adjustments

Thanks Mina. I like Option B as well — fairly low cost to us and strong customer stickiness. A couple of notes for Marissa / Legal: 

- Financials: Option B reduces revenue from surge by ~15% on the portion of minutes billed as surge. Using StormApps’ forecast (attached), the net impact over 12 months is ~4.5% revenue dilution but increases likelihood of a 12-mo commit.
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time credit up to 1,200 vGPU-minutes (equivalent to ~20 hours of a single A100 vGPU) with a cap of $2,700. Require signature on the commitment amendment. No separate SOW — the amendment will note the credit.
- Sustained-offset acceleration: approved if customer delivers telemetry feed (S3 export or Datadog link) for the 3-week window. We will include a clause that sustained-offset credit is retroactive only once telemetry verifies pattern.

If Marissa signs off, Mina can propose Option B with the 1,200-minute credit and the telemetry clause.

–Karthik
